title: Chapter 1
narration: Every image is a signal. A camera turns light into information, and a digital screen turns that information back into light.

title: Chapter 2
narration: A moving picture is really a sequence of images. Each frame can be examined on its own, without guessing what the camera recorded.

title: Chapter 3
narration: A digital image is a grid of samples. This original screen capture has a precise width and height, and every pixel has stored color values.

title: Chapter 4
narration: Instead of inventing numbers, we can measure the source directly. This report calculates the dimensions, pixel count and red, green and blue values of a single sample.

title: Chapter 5
narration: The same image can also become a texture. Here we averaged the colors into a smaller grid and mapped those values onto a curved three-dimensional surface.

title: Chapter 6
narration: From a single sample to a moving picture, from a flat image to a world: information becomes something we can see. Skelly Motion.
